spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od15m0p4t5 ----
\* A stock-exchange opening auction fills a bounded position book using optimistic locking with
\* retry. A trader reads the book's current version, then commits an added position only if the
\* version is unchanged and the book still has room under its capacity bound; a successful commit
\* bumps the version. If the version has moved on, the trader retries by re-reading. A privileged
\* admin may evict a filled position. The number of filled positions never exceeds the bound.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Slots == {0, 1, 2}
Traders == {0, 1}
Cap == 2
MaxV == 3

VARIABLES book, version, pend, clock

vars == <<book, version, pend, clock>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ book \in SUBSET Slots
    /\ version \in 0 .. MaxV
    /\ pend \in [Traders -> [rv : 0 .. MaxV, slot : Slots, on : BOOLEAN]]
    /\ clock \in {0, 1}

Init ==
    /\ book = {}
    /\ version = 0
    /\ pend = [t \in Traders |-> [rv |-> 0, slot |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ clock = 0

\* Optimistically read the version and stage a position to add.
Read(t, s) ==
    /\ ~pend[t].on
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![t] = [rv |-> version, slot |-> s, on |-> TRUE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, version, clock>>

\* Commit only if the version is unchanged and the book has room under the bound.
Commit(t) ==
    /\ pend[t].on
    /\ pend[t].rv = version
    /\ version < MaxV
    /\ pend[t].slot \notin book
    /\ Cardinality(book) < Cap
    /\ book' = book \cup {pend[t].slot}
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![t] = [rv |-> 0, slot |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

\* The version moved on: retry by re-reading, keeping the intended slot.
Retry(t) ==
    /\ pend[t].on
    /\ pend[t].rv # version
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![t] = [rv |-> version, slot |-> pend[t].slot, on |-> TRUE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, version, clock>>

\* Admin: evict a filled position from the book.
Evict(s) ==
    /\ s \in book
    /\ book' = book \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, pend, clock>>

\* Housekeeping pulse; always available.
Tick ==
    /\ clock' = 1 - clock
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, version, pend>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Traders, s \in Slots : Read(t, s)
    \/ \E t \in Traders : Commit(t) \/ Retry(t)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Evict(s)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Bounded capacity: the number of filled positions never exceeds the bound.
WithinBookCap == Cardinality(book) <= Cap
====
nl:
A stock-exchange opening auction fills a bounded position book using optimistic locking with
retry. A trader first reads the book's current version number and stages a position it wants to
add. It commits the addition only if the version is still unchanged and the book still has room
below its capacity bound; a successful commit inserts the position and bumps the version. If the
version has moved on since the read, the trader retries by re-reading the current version while
keeping the position it intended to add. A privileged admin may evict a filled position from the
book at any time. A housekeeping pulse ticks throughout.

Actions: optimistically read the version and stage a position to add; commit the staged position
when the version is unchanged and the book has room, bumping the version; retry by re-reading
when the version has moved on; admin-evict a filled position; tick the housekeeping pulse.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of filled positions in the book never exceeds the capacity bound.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od16m1p3t2 ----
\* A pharmacy prescription dispenser runs two instances that share one pool of dispensing bins,
\* with exclusive access governed by a ring token passed between the instances. Only the token
\* holder may allocate a free bin to a waiting prescription; allocation removes the bin from the
\* free pool and records its owner. Releasing a bin returns it to the free pool and clears its
\* owner. A bin is thus assigned to a prescription exactly when it is not in the free pool, so the
\* same bin is never handed to two prescriptions.
EXTENDS Naturals

Slots == {0, 1, 2}
Rx == {0, 1}
Inst == {"A", "B"}
NONE == 9

VARIABLES token, free, owner, pending

vars == <<token, free, owner, pending>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Inst
    /\ free \in SUBSET Slots
    /\ owner \in [Slots -> Rx \cup {NONE}]
    /\ pending \in SUBSET Rx

Init ==
    /\ token = "A"
    /\ free = Slots
    /\ owner = [s \in Slots |-> NONE]
    /\ pending = {}

\* Pass the ring token to the other instance; always available.
Pass ==
    /\ token' = IF token = "A" THEN "B" ELSE "A"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, owner, pending>>

\* A prescription arrives and waits for a bin.
Submit(r) ==
    /\ r \notin pending
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, free, owner>>

\* The token holder allocates a free bin to a waiting prescription, taking it out of the pool.
Allocate(s, r, i) ==
    /\ token = i
    /\ r \in pending
    /\ s \in free
    /\ owner[s] = NONE
    /\ free' = free \ {s}
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = r]
    /\ pending' = pending \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED token

\* Release a bin, returning it to the free pool and clearing its owner.
Release(s) ==
    /\ owner[s] # NONE
    /\ free' = free \cup {s}
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, pending>>

Next ==
    \/ Pass
    \/ \E r \in Rx : Submit(r)
    \/ \E s \in Slots, r \in Rx, i \in Inst : Allocate(s, r, i)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Release(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No double allocation: a bin is owned exactly when it is not in the free pool, so a bin can
\* never be handed out while it is still advertised as free (and thus grabbed twice).
FreeCoherent == \A s \in Slots : (owner[s] # NONE) <=> (s \notin free)
====
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser runs two independent instances that share one pool of
dispensing bins, with exclusive access to the pool governed by a ring token passed back and forth
between the two instances. A prescription arrives and waits for a bin. Only the instance currently
holding the ring token may allocate a free bin to a waiting prescription; allocating removes the
bin from the free pool and records the prescription as its owner. Releasing a bin returns it to
the free pool and clears its owner. Because a bin is recorded as owned exactly when it has been
taken out of the free pool, a bin can never be handed to a second prescription while it is still
advertised as free.

Actions: pass the ring token to the other instance; submit a prescription that waits for a bin;
the token holder allocates a free bin to a waiting prescription, removing it from the pool;
release a bin, returning it to the free pool and clearing its owner.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every bin is owned by a prescription exactly when it is not in the free pool, so
the same bin is never allocated to two prescriptions at once.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od15m1p1t0 ----
\* A stock-exchange opening auction lets only the trader holding the ring token touch the shared
\* fill counter. A holder reads the counter and stages a one-lot add against that reading, then
\* writes it back absolutely -- but passing the token discards any stage the leaving holder still
\* had, so a write always reflects the reading taken during the current, uninterrupted hold. One
\* trader may crash silently. The shared counter always equals the sum of each trader's own
\* contributions, so no committed add is ever lost by a stale write.
EXTENDS Naturals

Traders == {0, 1, 2}
N == 3
MaxTotal == 2

VARIABLES token, total, contrib, crashed, staged

vars == <<token, total, contrib, crashed, staged>>

Sum == contrib[0] + contrib[1] + contrib[2]

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Traders
    /\ total \in 0 .. MaxTotal
    /\ contrib \in [Traders -> 0 .. MaxTotal]
    /\ crashed \in SUBSET Traders
    /\ staged \in [Traders -> [base : 0 .. MaxTotal, on : BOOLEAN]]

Init ==
    /\ token = 0
    /\ total = 0
    /\ contrib = [t \in Traders |-> 0]
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ staged = [t \in Traders |-> [base |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]

\* Pass the ring token onward, discarding the leaving holder's staged write.
Pass ==
    /\ token' = (token + 1) % N
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![token] = [base |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<total, contrib, crashed>>

\* The token holder reads the counter and stages a one-lot add against that reading.
Read(t) ==
    /\ t = token
    /\ t \notin crashed
    /\ ~staged[t].on
    /\ total < MaxTotal
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![t] = [base |-> total, on |-> TRUE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, total, contrib, crashed>>

\* The holder writes its staged add back absolutely and records its own contribution.
Write(t) ==
    /\ t = token
    /\ staged[t].on
    /\ total' = staged[t].base + 1
    /\ contrib' = [contrib EXCEPT ![t] = contrib[t] + 1]
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![t] = [base |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, crashed>>

\* One trader may crash silently, dropping any staged write.
Crash(t) ==
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ crashed' = {t}
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![t] = [base |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, total, contrib>>

Next ==
    \/ Pass
    \/ \E t \in Traders : Read(t) \/ Write(t) \/ Crash(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No lost updates: the shared counter equals the sum of every trader's own contributions.
NoLostAdd == total = Sum
====
nl:
A stock-exchange opening auction lets only the trader currently holding the ring token touch the
shared fill counter. A holder reads the counter and stages a one-lot add computed from that
reading, then writes the new value back absolutely. Passing the ring token onward discards any
staged write the leaving holder still had, so a write always reflects the reading the holder took
during its current, uninterrupted hold of the token. One trader may crash silently, dropping any
staged write it had. Each trader also keeps a tally of its own contributions. Because only the
token holder writes and a stage cannot survive a token pass, no add based on a stale reading can
overwrite the counter, and no committed add is lost.

Actions: pass the ring token onward, discarding the leaving holder's staged write; the token
holder reads the counter and stages a one-lot add; the holder writes its staged add back
absolutely and records its own contribution; one trader crashes silently, dropping its stage.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared fill counter always equals the sum of every trader's own recorded
contributions, so no committed add is ever lost by a stale write.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od12m8p4t1 ----
\* A blood-bank inventory tracker guards its fridges with hierarchical locks: a coarse fridge
\* lock and a fine per-shelf lock. Storing a unit onto a shelf requires holding both the fridge
\* lock and that shelf's lock, and is only allowed while the shelf is below its capacity bound.
\* Store orders arrive in an inbox and may be honoured out of order. Units may also be withdrawn.
\* No shelf ever holds more units than its capacity bound.
EXTENDS Naturals

Shelves == {0, 1}
Workers == {0, 1}
FREE == 9
Cap == 2

VARIABLES fridgeLock, shelfLock, stored, inbox, clock

vars == <<fridgeLock, shelfLock, stored, inbox, clock>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ fridgeLock \in Workers \cup {FREE}
    /\ shelfLock \in [Shelves -> Workers \cup {FREE}]
    /\ stored \in [Shelves -> 0 .. Cap]
    /\ inbox \in SUBSET Shelves
    /\ clock \in {0, 1}

Init ==
    /\ fridgeLock = FREE
    /\ shelfLock = [s \in Shelves |-> FREE]
    /\ stored = [s \in Shelves |-> 0]
    /\ inbox = {}
    /\ clock = 0

\* A store order for a shelf arrives in the inbox (may be honoured out of order later).
Request(s) ==
    /\ s \notin inbox
    /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridgeLock, shelfLock, stored, clock>>

\* Grab the coarse fridge lock.
GrabFridge(w) ==
    /\ fridgeLock = FREE
    /\ fridgeLock' = w
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelfLock, stored, inbox, clock>>

\* Grab a shelf's fine lock while holding the fridge lock.
GrabShelf(s, w) ==
    /\ fridgeLock = w
    /\ shelfLock[s] = FREE
    /\ shelfLock' = [shelfLock EXCEPT ![s] = w]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridgeLock, stored, inbox, clock>>

\* Store a unit onto a shelf, holding both locks and below the shelf's capacity bound.
Store(s, w) ==
    /\ fridgeLock = w
    /\ shelfLock[s] = w
    /\ s \in inbox
    /\ stored[s] < Cap
    /\ stored' = [stored EXCEPT ![s] = stored[s] + 1]
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridgeLock, shelfLock, clock>>

\* Withdraw a unit from a shelf.
Withdraw(s) ==
    /\ stored[s] > 0
    /\ stored' = [stored EXCEPT ![s] = stored[s] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridgeLock, shelfLock, inbox, clock>>

\* Release a shelf lock.
ReleaseShelf(s, w) ==
    /\ shelfLock[s] = w
    /\ shelfLock' = [shelfLock EXCEPT ![s] = FREE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridgeLock, stored, inbox, clock>>

\* Release the fridge lock once no shelf is still locked by this worker.
ReleaseFridge(w) ==
    /\ fridgeLock = w
    /\ \A s \in Shelves : shelfLock[s] # w
    /\ fridgeLock' = FREE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelfLock, stored, inbox, clock>>

\* Housekeeping pulse; always available.
Tick ==
    /\ clock' = 1 - clock
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridgeLock, shelfLock, stored, inbox>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Shelves : Request(s) \/ Withdraw(s)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : GrabFridge(w) \/ ReleaseFridge(w)
    \/ \E s \in Shelves, w \in Workers : GrabShelf(s, w) \/ Store(s, w) \/ ReleaseShelf(s, w)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Bounded capacity: no shelf ever holds more units than its capacity bound.
WithinShelfCap == \A s \in Shelves : stored[s] <= Cap
====
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker guards its fridges with two levels of hierarchical locks: a coarse
lock over a fridge and a fine lock over each shelf. To store a unit onto a shelf, a worker must
hold both the fridge lock and that shelf's lock, and the store is allowed only while the shelf is
below its capacity bound. Store orders arrive in an inbox and may be honoured out of order, so the
order in which shelves are stocked need not match the order the orders came in. Units may also be
withdrawn from a shelf. A worker cannot release a fridge lock while it still holds any shelf lock
inside that fridge. A housekeeping pulse ticks throughout.

Actions: a store order for a shelf arrives in the inbox; grab the coarse fridge lock; grab a
shelf's fine lock while holding the fridge lock; store a unit onto a shelf while holding both locks
and below capacity, consuming its order; withdraw a unit from a shelf; release a shelf lock;
release the fridge lock once no shelf is still locked by the worker; tick the housekeeping pulse.

SAFETY PROPERTY: no shelf ever holds more units than its capacity bound.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od15m3p2t4 ----
\* A stock-exchange opening auction, coordinated by an elected leader (with failover to a new
\* term), keeps a fixed quantity of shares distributed across three books: available, locked, and
\* executed. The leader locks available shares for matching -- bounded by a runtime-adjustable
\* capacity -- executes locked shares, or unlocks them back to available. Shares are conserved:
\* the three books always sum to the fixed total, no share created or destroyed.
EXTENDS Naturals

Total == 3
MaxTerm == 1
MaxCap == 3

VARIABLES avail, locked, executed, capacity, term

vars == <<avail, locked, executed, capacity, term>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ avail \in 0 .. Total
    /\ locked \in 0 .. Total
    /\ executed \in 0 .. Total
    /\ capacity \in 0 .. MaxCap
    /\ term \in 0 .. MaxTerm

Init ==
    /\ avail = Total
    /\ locked = 0
    /\ executed = 0
    /\ capacity = MaxCap
    /\ term = 0

\* Failover: elect a fresh leader term, cycling within a bounded band.
Elect ==
    /\ term' = (term + 1) % (MaxTerm + 1)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<avail, locked, executed, capacity>>

\* Lock available shares for matching, staying within the current capacity.
Lock(k) ==
    /\ k > 0
    /\ k <= avail
    /\ locked + k <= capacity
    /\ avail' = avail - k
    /\ locked' = locked + k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<executed, capacity, term>>

\* Execute locked shares, moving them to the executed book.
Execute(k) ==
    /\ k > 0
    /\ k <= locked
    /\ locked' = locked - k
    /\ executed' = executed + k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<avail, capacity, term>>

\* Unlock shares back to the available book.
Unlock(k) ==
    /\ k > 0
    /\ k <= locked
    /\ locked' = locked - k
    /\ avail' = avail + k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<executed, capacity, term>>

\* Capacity changes at runtime to a different value; always available.
Resize(c) ==
    /\ c # capacity
    /\ capacity' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<avail, locked, executed, term>>

Next ==
    \/ Elect
    \/ \E k \in 1 .. Total : Lock(k) \/ Execute(k) \/ Unlock(k)
    \/ \E c \in 0 .. MaxCap : Resize(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Conservation: available, locked, and executed shares always sum to the fixed total.
SharesConserved == avail + locked + executed = Total
====
nl:
A stock-exchange opening auction is coordinated by an elected leader that fails over to a fresh
term when needed. It keeps a fixed quantity of shares distributed across three books: available,
locked, and executed. The leader locks available shares for matching, but only so far as the
locked total stays within a capacity that can be adjusted at runtime. Locked shares may then be
executed, moving them into the executed book, or unlocked, moving them back to available. The
capacity may be resized at runtime to a different value. No share is ever created or destroyed.

Actions: fail over by electing a fresh leader term; lock available shares for matching while
within capacity; execute locked shares into the executed book; unlock locked shares back to
available; resize the matching capacity at runtime.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the available, locked, and executed share counts always sum to the fixed total,
so no share is ever created or destroyed.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od13m1p1t5 ----
\* A vending-machine network shares one mechanical vend meter, writable only by the machine
\* holding the ring token. A holder reads the meter and later writes it back as the read value
\* plus one, logging the vend. Passing the token discards any read the leaving holder still had,
\* so a write reflects the meter as read during the current, uninterrupted hold. A privileged
\* admin may override, clearing all outstanding reads. The meter always equals the number of
\* vends recorded in the log, so no vend is lost by a stale write.
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

Machines == {0, 1}
N == 2
MaxVends == 3

VARIABLES token, meter, vendLog, staged

vars == <<token, meter, vendLog, staged>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Machines
    /\ meter \in 0 .. MaxVends
    /\ vendLog \in Seq(Machines)
    /\ staged \in [Machines -> [rm : 0 .. MaxVends, on : BOOLEAN]]

Init ==
    /\ token = 0
    /\ meter = 0
    /\ vendLog = <<>>
    /\ staged = [m \in Machines |-> [rm |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]

\* Pass the ring token, discarding the leaving holder's staged read.
Pass ==
    /\ token' = (token + 1) % N
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![token] = [rm |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<meter, vendLog>>

\* The token holder reads the current meter value.
Read(m) ==
    /\ m = token
    /\ ~staged[m].on
    /\ meter < MaxVends
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![m] = [rm |-> meter, on |-> TRUE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, meter, vendLog>>

\* The holder writes the meter back as its read value plus one, logging the vend.
Vend(m) ==
    /\ m = token
    /\ staged[m].on
    /\ Len(vendLog) < MaxVends
    /\ meter' = staged[m].rm + 1
    /\ vendLog' = Append(vendLog, m)
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![m] = [rm |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED token

\* Admin override: clear all outstanding reads; always available.
Override ==
    /\ staged' = [m \in Machines |-> [rm |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, meter, vendLog>>

Next ==
    \/ Pass
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Read(m) \/ Vend(m)
    \/ Override

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No lost updates: the meter equals the number of vends recorded in the log.
NoLostVend == meter = Len(vendLog)
====
nl:
A vending-machine network shares a single mechanical vend meter, which may be written only by the
machine currently holding the ring token. A holder first reads the current meter value. Later it
writes the meter back as the value it read plus one, and logs the vend. Passing the ring token
onward discards any read the leaving holder still had outstanding, so a write always reflects the
meter value as it was read during the holder's current, uninterrupted hold of the token. A
privileged admin may override at any time, clearing all outstanding reads. Because a stale read
cannot survive a token pass, no vend based on an out-of-date meter reading can overwrite the meter
and lose a vend.

Actions: pass the ring token, discarding the leaving holder's staged read; the token holder reads
the current meter; the holder writes the meter back as its read value plus one and logs the vend;
admin-override to clear all outstanding reads.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the vend meter always equals the number of vends recorded in the log, so no vend
is ever lost by a stale write.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od1m7p2t3 ----
\* An air-traffic runway allocator exposes its free-slot count as a compare-and-swap register.
\* A controller reads the free count, stages an assignment to a runway, and commits only if the
\* free count is still on the value it read; the commit writes the free count absolutely as the
\* read value minus one and adds a slot to that runway. A slow controller whose reading is stale
\* simply retries. Slots are conserved: free slots plus slots assigned across the runways always
\* total the fixed pool.
EXTENDS Naturals

Runways == {0, 1}
Controllers == {0, 1}
Total == 3

VARIABLES free, assigned, attempt, clock

vars == <<free, assigned, attempt, clock>>

Sum == assigned[0] + assigned[1]

TypeOK ==
    /\ free \in 0 .. Total
    /\ assigned \in [Runways -> 0 .. Total]
    /\ attempt \in [Controllers -> [exp : 0 .. Total, rw : Runways, on : BOOLEAN]]
    /\ clock \in {0, 1}

Init ==
    /\ free = Total
    /\ assigned = [r \in Runways |-> 0]
    /\ attempt = [c \in Controllers |-> [exp |-> 0, rw |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ clock = 0

\* A controller reads the free count and stages an assignment to a runway.
Read(c, r) ==
    /\ ~attempt[c].on
    /\ free > 0
    /\ attempt' = [attempt EXCEPT ![c] = [exp |-> free, rw |-> r, on |-> TRUE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, assigned, clock>>

\* Commit only if the free count is still on the read value; write it absolutely, assign a slot.
Commit(c) ==
    /\ attempt[c].on
    /\ attempt[c].exp = free
    /\ free > 0
    /\ free' = attempt[c].exp - 1
    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![attempt[c].rw] = assigned[attempt[c].rw] + 1]
    /\ attempt' = [attempt EXCEPT ![c] = [exp |-> 0, rw |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

\* A slow controller whose reading is stale retries by re-reading, keeping its target runway.
Retry(c) ==
    /\ attempt[c].on
    /\ attempt[c].exp # free
    /\ attempt' = [attempt EXCEPT ![c] = [exp |-> free, rw |-> attempt[c].rw, on |-> TRUE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, assigned, clock>>

\* Release a slot from a runway back to the free pool.
Release(r) ==
    /\ assigned[r] > 0
    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![r] = assigned[r] - 1]
    /\ free' = free + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<attempt, clock>>

\* Timing pulse standing in for the passage of time; always available.
Tick ==
    /\ clock' = 1 - clock
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, assigned, attempt>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, r \in Runways : Read(c, r)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Commit(c) \/ Retry(c)
    \/ \E r \in Runways : Release(r)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Conservation: free slots plus slots assigned across all runways always total the pool.
SlotsConserved == free + Sum = Total
====
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator exposes its count of free departure slots as a single
compare-and-swap register. A controller first reads the free-slot count and stages an assignment
of a slot to a particular runway, remembering the count it read. It commits the assignment only
if the free count is still sitting on exactly the value it read; the commit then writes the free
count back absolutely as that read value minus one and adds a slot to the chosen runway. A slow
controller whose reading has gone stale -- because the free count moved on before it committed --
simply retries by re-reading, keeping the runway it intended. A slot assigned to a runway may be
released back to the free pool. Slots are neither created nor destroyed.

Actions: read the free count and stage a runway assignment; commit an assignment when the free
count still matches the reading, writing the count absolutely and assigning a slot; retry by
re-reading when the reading is stale; release a slot from a runway to the free pool; tick the clock.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the free slots plus the slots assigned across all runways always total the fixed
pool, so no slot is ever created or destroyed by a stale write.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od19m8p4t4 ----
\* A library book-reservation system guards reservations with hierarchical locks: a coarse catalog
\* lock and a fine per-copy lock. A member reserves a copy only while holding both the catalog lock
\* and that copy's lock, and only while the total number of reservations is below a capacity bound.
\* The capacity may be adjusted at runtime, but never below the number of copies already reserved.
\* The total number of reserved copies never exceeds the capacity bound.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Copies == {0, 1, 2}
Members == {0, 1}
FREE == 9
MaxCap == 3

VARIABLES catalogLock, copyLock, reserved, capacity, clock

vars == <<catalogLock, copyLock, reserved, capacity, clock>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ catalogLock \in Members \cup {FREE}
    /\ copyLock \in [Copies -> Members \cup {FREE}]
    /\ reserved \in SUBSET Copies
    /\ capacity \in 0 .. MaxCap
    /\ clock \in {0, 1}

Init ==
    /\ catalogLock = FREE
    /\ copyLock = [c \in Copies |-> FREE]
    /\ reserved = {}
    /\ capacity = MaxCap
    /\ clock = 0

\* Grab the coarse catalog lock.
GrabCatalog(m) ==
    /\ catalogLock = FREE
    /\ catalogLock' = m
    /\ UNCHANGED <<copyLock, reserved, capacity, clock>>

\* Grab a copy's fine lock while holding the catalog lock.
GrabCopy(c, m) ==
    /\ catalogLock = m
    /\ copyLock[c] = FREE
    /\ copyLock' = [copyLock EXCEPT ![c] = m]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<catalogLock, reserved, capacity, clock>>

\* Reserve a copy while holding both locks and below the capacity bound.
Reserve(c, m) ==
    /\ catalogLock = m
    /\ copyLock[c] = m
    /\ c \notin reserved
    /\ Cardinality(reserved) < capacity
    /\ reserved' = reserved \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<catalogLock, copyLock, capacity, clock>>

\* Cancel a reservation.
Cancel(c) ==
    /\ c \in reserved
    /\ reserved' = reserved \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<catalogLock, copyLock, capacity, clock>>

\* Release a copy lock.
ReleaseCopy(c, m) ==
    /\ copyLock[c] = m
    /\ copyLock' = [copyLock EXCEPT ![c] = FREE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<catalogLock, reserved, capacity, clock>>

\* Release the catalog lock once no copy is still locked by this member.
ReleaseCatalog(m) ==
    /\ catalogLock = m
    /\ \A c \in Copies : copyLock[c] # m
    /\ catalogLock' = FREE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<copyLock, reserved, capacity, clock>>

\* Capacity changes at runtime, but never below the number already reserved.
Resize(k) ==
    /\ k # capacity
    /\ k >= Cardinality(reserved)
    /\ capacity' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<catalogLock, copyLock, reserved, clock>>

\* Housekeeping pulse; always available.
Tick ==
    /\ clock' = 1 - clock
    /\ UNCHANGED <<catalogLock, copyLock, reserved, capacity>>

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Members : GrabCatalog(m) \/ ReleaseCatalog(m)
    \/ \E c \in Copies, m \in Members : GrabCopy(c, m) \/ Reserve(c, m) \/ ReleaseCopy(c, m)
    \/ \E c \in Copies : Cancel(c)
    \/ \E k \in 0 .. MaxCap : Resize(k)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Bounded capacity: the number of reserved copies never exceeds the capacity bound.
WithinResCap == Cardinality(reserved) <= capacity
====
nl:
A library book-reservation system guards its reservations with two levels of hierarchical locks:
a coarse catalog lock and a fine per-copy lock. A member may reserve a copy only while holding
both the catalog lock and that copy's lock, and only while the total number of reservations across
the whole library is below a capacity bound. The capacity may be adjusted at runtime to a
different value, but it is never lowered below the number of copies already reserved. A member
cannot release the catalog lock while it still holds any copy lock. Reservations may be cancelled,
and a housekeeping pulse ticks throughout.

Actions: grab the coarse catalog lock; grab a copy's fine lock while holding the catalog lock;
reserve a copy while holding both locks and below capacity; cancel a reservation; release a copy
lock; release the catalog lock once no copy is still locked by the member; resize the capacity at
runtime, never below current occupancy; tick the housekeeping pulse.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the total number of reserved copies never exceeds the capacity bound.

---- MODULE W4Od5m5p3t4 ----
\* A multiplayer lobby matchmaker allocates seats by quorum vote. For each seat a player is
\* nominated, others vote, and a strict majority elects a unique winner for that seat. Only that
\* winner may be allocated the seat, and only while the total seats allocated stays under a
\* runtime-adjustable capacity. Because a seat is only ever held by its quorum-elected winner, the
\* same seat is never allocated to two different players.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Seats == {0, 1}
Players == {0, 1, 2}
NONE == 9
MaxCap == 2

VARIABLES nominee, votes, winner, owner, capacity

vars == <<nominee, votes, winner, owner, capacity>>

Owned == Cardinality({s \in Seats : owner[s] # NONE})

TypeOK ==
    /\ nominee \in [Seats -> Players \cup {NONE}]
    /\ votes \in [Seats -> SUBSET Players]
    /\ winner \in [Seats -> Players \cup {NONE}]
    /\ owner \in [Seats -> Players \cup {NONE}]
    /\ capacity \in 0 .. MaxCap

Init ==
    /\ nominee = [s \in Seats |-> NONE]
    /\ votes = [s \in Seats |-> {}]
    /\ winner = [s \in Seats |-> NONE]
    /\ owner = [s \in Seats |-> NONE]
    /\ capacity = MaxCap

\* Nominate a player for a free, uncontested seat, resetting its tally.
Nominate(s, p) ==
    /\ nominee[s] = NONE
    /\ winner[s] = NONE
    /\ owner[s] = NONE
    /\ nominee' = [nominee EXCEPT ![s] = p]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<winner, owner, capacity>>

\* A player votes for a seat's nominee.
Vote(s, v) ==
    /\ nominee[s] # NONE
    /\ v \notin votes[s]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = votes[s] \cup {v}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<nominee, winner, owner, capacity>>

\* A strict majority elects the nominee as the seat's unique winner.
Elect(s) ==
    /\ nominee[s] # NONE
    /\ 2 * Cardinality(votes[s]) > Cardinality(Players)
    /\ winner' = [winner EXCEPT ![s] = nominee[s]]
    /\ nominee' = [nominee EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, owner, capacity>>

\* Allocate the seat to its elected winner, while under the capacity bound.
Allocate(s) ==
    /\ winner[s] # NONE
    /\ owner[s] = NONE
    /\ Owned < capacity
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = winner[s]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<nominee, votes, winner, capacity>>

\* Release a seat, clearing its holder, winner, and votes.
Release(s) ==
    /\ owner[s] # NONE
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
    /\ winner' = [winner EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<nominee, capacity>>

\* Capacity changes at runtime to a different value; always available.
Resize(c) ==
    /\ c # capacity
    /\ capacity' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<nominee, votes, winner, owner>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Seats, p \in Players : Nominate(s, p)
    \/ \E s \in Seats, v \in Players : Vote(s, v)
    \/ \E s \in Seats : Elect(s) \/ Allocate(s) \/ Release(s)
    \/ \E c \in 0 .. MaxCap : Resize(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No double allocation: a held seat is held by its quorum-elected winner, so it cannot also be
\* allocated to any other player.
NoDoubleSeat == \A s \in Seats : owner[s] # NONE => owner[s] = winner[s]
====
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker allocates seats by quorum vote. For each seat, a player is
nominated for the free seat, which resets that seat's vote tally; other players then vote for the
nominee. Once a strict majority has voted, the nominee is elected as that seat's unique winner.
Only that elected winner may then be allocated the seat, and only while the total number of seats
already allocated stays below a capacity that can be adjusted at runtime. Releasing a seat clears
its holder, its winner, and its votes. Because a seat is only ever held by the winner a quorum
elected for it, the same seat can never be allocated to two different players.

Actions: nominate a player for a free uncontested seat, resetting its tally; a player votes for a
seat's nominee; elect a nominee with a strict majority as the seat's winner; allocate a seat to its
elected winner while under capacity; release a seat, clearing its holder, winner, and votes; resize
the capacity at runtime.

SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a seat is held, it is held by the player a quorum elected as its winner,
so no seat is ever double-allocated to two players at once.

---- MODULE W4Od16m4p2t4 ----
\* A pharmacy prescription dispenser moves a fixed set of prescriptions through a pipeline of four
\* stages: pending, queued, processing, and dispensed. Enqueuing applies backpressure -- a pending
\* prescription joins the bounded work queue only while the queue is below its capacity, and that
\* capacity may change at runtime. Prescriptions then move to processing and finally to dispensed.
\* No prescription is created or destroyed: the four stages always sum to the fixed total.
EXTENDS Naturals

Total == 3
MaxCap == 3

VARIABLES pending, queued, processing, dispensed, capacity

vars == <<pending, queued, processing, dispensed, capacity>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ pending \in 0 .. Total
    /\ queued \in 0 .. Total
    /\ processing \in 0 .. Total
    /\ dispensed \in 0 .. Total
    /\ capacity \in 0 .. MaxCap

Init ==
    /\ pending = Total
    /\ queued = 0
    /\ processing = 0
    /\ dispensed = 0
    /\ capacity = MaxCap

\* Enqueue a pending prescription under backpressure: only while the queue is below capacity.
Enqueue ==
    /\ pending > 0
    /\ queued < capacity
    /\ pending' = pending - 1
    /\ queued' = queued + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<processing, dispensed, capacity>>

\* Pull a queued prescription into processing.
StartProcess ==
    /\ queued > 0
    /\ queued' = queued - 1
    /\ processing' = processing + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, dispensed, capacity>>

\* Finish processing a prescription, dispensing it.
Dispense ==
    /\ processing > 0
    /\ processing' = processing - 1
    /\ dispensed' = dispensed + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, queued, capacity>>

\* Return a dispensed prescription to pending (e.g. a refill cycle).
Recycle ==
    /\ dispensed > 0
    /\ dispensed' = dispensed - 1
    /\ pending' = pending + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queued, processing, capacity>>

\* The queue capacity changes at runtime to a different value; always available.
Resize(c) ==
    /\ c # capacity
    /\ capacity' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, queued, processing, dispensed>>

Next ==
    \/ Enqueue
    \/ StartProcess
    \/ Dispense
    \/ Recycle
    \/ \E c \in 0 .. MaxCap : Resize(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Conservation: the four pipeline stages always sum to the fixed total of prescriptions.
RxConserved == pending + queued + processing + dispensed = Total
====
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser moves a fixed set of prescriptions through a pipeline of four
stages: pending, queued, processing, and dispensed. Enqueuing applies backpressure -- a pending
prescription may join the bounded work queue only while the queue is below its capacity, and that
capacity may itself change at runtime. A queued prescription is pulled into processing, and a
processed prescription is finally dispensed. A dispensed prescription may be recycled back to
pending, standing in for a refill cycle. At no point is a prescription created or destroyed.

Actions: enqueue a pending prescription under backpressure while the queue is below capacity;
pull a queued prescription into processing; dispense a processed prescription; recycle a dispensed
prescription back to pending; resize the queue capacity at runtime.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the counts of pending, queued, processing, and dispensed prescriptions always sum
to the fixed total, so no prescription is ever created or destroyed.

---- MODULE W4Od4m8p4t4 ----
\* A car-wash conveyor line guards its bays with hierarchical locks: a coarse line lock and a fine
\* per-bay lock. A car enters a bay only while a crew holds both the line lock and that bay's lock,
\* and only while the bay is below its per-bay capacity. That per-bay capacity may be adjusted at
\* runtime, but never below the occupancy of any bay. Cars exit bays, and a crew cannot drop the
\* line lock while still holding a bay lock. No bay ever holds more cars than the capacity bound.
EXTENDS Naturals

Bays == {0, 1}
Crews == {0, 1}
FREE == 9
MaxCap == 2

VARIABLES lineLock, bayLock, occupancy, bayCap, clock

vars == <<lineLock, bayLock, occupancy, bayCap, clock>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ lineLock \in Crews \cup {FREE}
    /\ bayLock \in [Bays -> Crews \cup {FREE}]
    /\ occupancy \in [Bays -> 0 .. MaxCap]
    /\ bayCap \in 0 .. MaxCap
    /\ clock \in {0, 1}

Init ==
    /\ lineLock = FREE
    /\ bayLock = [b \in Bays |-> FREE]
    /\ occupancy = [b \in Bays |-> 0]
    /\ bayCap = MaxCap
    /\ clock = 0

\* Grab the coarse line lock.
GrabLine(w) ==
    /\ lineLock = FREE
    /\ lineLock' = w
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bayLock, occupancy, bayCap, clock>>

\* Grab a bay's fine lock while holding the line lock.
GrabBay(b, w) ==
    /\ lineLock = w
    /\ bayLock[b] = FREE
    /\ bayLock' = [bayLock EXCEPT ![b] = w]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lineLock, occupancy, bayCap, clock>>

\* A car enters a bay while both locks are held and the bay is below its capacity.
Enter(b, w) ==
    /\ lineLock = w
    /\ bayLock[b] = w
    /\ occupancy[b] < bayCap
    /\ occupancy' = [occupancy EXCEPT ![b] = occupancy[b] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lineLock, bayLock, bayCap, clock>>

\* A car exits a bay.
Exit(b) ==
    /\ occupancy[b] > 0
    /\ occupancy' = [occupancy EXCEPT ![b] = occupancy[b] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lineLock, bayLock, bayCap, clock>>

\* Release a bay lock.
ReleaseBay(b, w) ==
    /\ bayLock[b] = w
    /\ bayLock' = [bayLock EXCEPT ![b] = FREE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lineLock, occupancy, bayCap, clock>>

\* Release the line lock once no bay is still locked by this crew.
ReleaseLine(w) ==
    /\ lineLock = w
    /\ \A b \in Bays : bayLock[b] # w
    /\ lineLock' = FREE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bayLock, occupancy, bayCap, clock>>

\* Per-bay capacity changes at runtime, but never below any bay's occupancy.
Resize(k) ==
    /\ k # bayCap
    /\ \A b \in Bays : occupancy[b] <= k
    /\ bayCap' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lineLock, bayLock, occupancy, clock>>

\* Conveyor pulse; always available.
Tick ==
    /\ clock' = 1 - clock
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lineLock, bayLock, occupancy, bayCap>>

Next ==
    \/ \E w \in Crews : GrabLine(w) \/ ReleaseLine(w)
    \/ \E b \in Bays, w \in Crews : GrabBay(b, w) \/ Enter(b, w) \/ ReleaseBay(b, w)
    \/ \E b \in Bays : Exit(b)
    \/ \E k \in 0 .. MaxCap : Resize(k)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Bounded capacity: no bay ever holds more cars than the per-bay capacity bound.
WithinBayCap == \A b \in Bays : occupancy[b] <= bayCap
====
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line guards its wash bays with two levels of hierarchical locks: a coarse line
lock and a fine per-bay lock. A car may enter a bay only while a crew holds both the line lock and
that bay's lock, and only while the bay is currently below its per-bay capacity. The per-bay
capacity may be adjusted at runtime to a different value, but it is never lowered below the current
occupancy of any bay. Cars exit bays freely. A crew cannot release the line lock while it still
holds any bay lock. A conveyor pulse ticks throughout.

Actions: grab the coarse line lock; grab a bay's fine lock while holding the line lock; a car
enters a bay while both locks are held and the bay is below capacity; a car exits a bay; release a
bay lock; release the line lock once no bay is still locked by the crew; resize the per-bay
capacity at runtime, never below any bay's occupancy; tick the conveyor pulse.

SAFETY PROPERTY: no bay ever holds more cars than the per-bay capacity bound.

---- MODULE W4Od12m2p1t0 ----
\* A blood-bank inventory tracker updates its shared stock through two-phase commit. Preparing a
\* transaction acquires the single write lock and reads the current stock as the transaction's
\* base; committing writes the stock back absolutely as that base plus one and logs the unit.
\* Because the write lock serializes preparers, a commit's base is never stale, so no update is
\* lost. One participant may crash silently, releasing any lock it held. The stock always equals
\* the total of the units logged.
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

TX == {0, 1}
NONE == 9
MaxStock == 3
MaxLog == 3

VARIABLES stock, writeLock, prep, log, crashed, clock

vars == <<stock, writeLock, prep, log, crashed, clock>>

RECURSIVE Total(_)
Total(s) == IF s = <<>> THEN 0 ELSE Head(s) + Total(Tail(s))

TypeOK ==
    /\ stock \in 0 .. MaxStock
    /\ writeLock \in TX \cup {NONE}
    /\ prep \in [TX -> [base : 0 .. MaxStock, on : BOOLEAN]]
    /\ log \in Seq({1})
    /\ crashed \in SUBSET TX
    /\ clock \in {0, 1}

Init ==
    /\ stock = 0
    /\ writeLock = NONE
    /\ prep = [t \in TX |-> [base |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ log = <<>>
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ clock = 0

\* Prepare: acquire the write lock and read the current stock as the base.
Prepare(t) ==
    /\ writeLock = NONE
    /\ t \notin crashed
    /\ ~prep[t].on
    /\ stock < MaxStock
    /\ writeLock' = t
    /\ prep' = [prep EXCEPT ![t] = [base |-> stock, on |-> TRUE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, log, crashed, clock>>

\* Commit: write the stock back absolutely as base plus one and log the unit; release the lock.
Commit(t) ==
    /\ writeLock = t
    /\ prep[t].on
    /\ Len(log) < MaxLog
    /\ stock' = prep[t].base + 1
    /\ log' = Append(log, 1)
    /\ prep' = [prep EXCEPT ![t] = [base |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ writeLock' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, clock>>

\* Abort: release the write lock without committing.
Abort(t) ==
    /\ writeLock = t
    /\ prep[t].on
    /\ prep' = [prep EXCEPT ![t] = [base |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ writeLock' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, log, crashed, clock>>

\* One participant crashes silently, releasing any lock and preparation it held.
Crash(t) ==
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ crashed' = {t}
    /\ prep' = [prep EXCEPT ![t] = [base |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ writeLock' = IF writeLock = t THEN NONE ELSE writeLock
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, log, clock>>

\* Housekeeping pulse; always available.
Tick ==
    /\ clock' = 1 - clock
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, writeLock, prep, log, crashed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in TX : Prepare(t) \/ Commit(t) \/ Abort(t) \/ Crash(t)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No lost updates: the shared stock equals the total of every unit recorded in the log.
NoLostUnit == stock = Total(log)
====
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker updates its shared stock count through two-phase commit. Preparing a
transaction acquires the single write lock and reads the current stock as that transaction's base
value. Committing then writes the stock back absolutely as the base plus one, and appends the unit
to a log; committing releases the write lock. A prepared transaction may instead be aborted,
releasing the lock without changing the stock. Because the write lock serializes preparers, a
committing transaction's base reading is never stale, so no committed update is lost. One
participant may crash silently, releasing any write lock and preparation it was holding. A
housekeeping pulse ticks throughout.

Actions: prepare a transaction, acquiring the write lock and reading the base stock; commit,
writing the stock absolutely as base plus one and logging the unit; abort, releasing the lock
without committing; crash one participant silently, releasing its lock and preparation; tick the
housekeeping pulse.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared stock count always equals the total of every unit recorded in the log,
so no committed update is ever lost by a stale write.

---- MODULE W4Od2m9p0t3 ----
\* A warehouse robot fleet coordinates exclusive access to a critical charging zone with a single
\* physical key, reissued each epoch. A robot requests the zone, takes the key while it is free,
\* and enters the zone only while holding the key. A robot may be slow to leave -- nothing forces
\* it out -- but it is never failed. Reconfiguring to a new epoch clears the key, the occupant, and
\* all requests. Whoever is inside the zone holds the key, so two robots are never inside at once.
EXTENDS Naturals

Robots == {0, 1, 2}
NONE == 9
MaxEpoch == 2

VARIABLES epoch, key, owner, requests

vars == <<epoch, key, owner, requests>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
    /\ key \in Robots \cup {NONE}
    /\ owner \in Robots \cup {NONE}
    /\ requests \in SUBSET Robots

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ key = NONE
    /\ owner = NONE
    /\ requests = {}

\* Reconfigure to the next epoch, clearing the key, the occupant, and all requests.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch' = (epoch + 1) % (MaxEpoch + 1)
    /\ key' = NONE
    /\ owner' = NONE
    /\ requests' = {}

\* A robot requests the critical zone.
Request(r) ==
    /\ r \notin requests
    /\ requests' = requests \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, key, owner>>

\* A requesting robot takes the key while it is free.
TakeKey(r) ==
    /\ key = NONE
    /\ r \in requests
    /\ key' = r
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owner, requests>>

\* A robot enters the zone only while it holds the key.
Enter(r) ==
    /\ key = r
    /\ owner = NONE
    /\ owner' = r
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, key, requests>>

\* The occupant leaves the zone (it may be slow to do so, but is never failed).
Exit(r) ==
    /\ owner = r
    /\ owner' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, key, requests>>

\* A robot not inside the zone drops the key, clearing its request.
DropKey(r) ==
    /\ key = r
    /\ owner # r
    /\ key' = NONE
    /\ requests' = requests \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owner>>

Next ==
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Request(r) \/ TakeKey(r) \/ Enter(r) \/ Exit(r) \/ DropKey(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Mutual exclusion: whoever is inside the critical zone holds the single key, so two robots can
\* never be inside the zone at the same time.
MutexByKey == owner # NONE => key = owner
====
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet coordinates exclusive access to a single critical charging zone using one
physical key, which is reissued each epoch. A robot first requests the zone. While the key is free,
a requesting robot may take it, and a robot may enter the zone only while it is holding the key. A
robot inside the zone may be slow to leave -- nothing forces it out -- but it is never treated as
failed. A robot that is not inside the zone may drop the key, clearing its request. Reconfiguring
to the next epoch clears the key, the current occupant, and all outstanding requests.

Actions: reconfigure to the next epoch, clearing key, occupant, and requests; request the zone;
take the free key while requesting; enter the zone while holding the key; leave the zone; drop the
key while not inside, clearing the request.

SAFETY PROPERTY: whoever is inside the critical charging zone is holding the single key, so two
robots are never inside the zone at the same time.

---- MODULE W4Od2m1p2t2 ----
\* Two warehouse-robot conveyor instances share one item pool, with exclusive handling granted by
\* a ring token passed between them. The token holder grabs an item from the shared pool into
\* transit, then deposits it into its own conveyor loop. Items in a loop may be released back to
\* the shared pool. Items are conserved across four places: the shared pool, each instance's loop,
\* and transit -- none created or destroyed.
EXTENDS Naturals

Inst == {"A", "B"}
Total == 3

VARIABLES token, pool, loop, inTransit

vars == <<token, pool, loop, inTransit>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Inst
    /\ pool \in 0 .. Total
    /\ loop \in [Inst -> 0 .. Total]
    /\ inTransit \in 0 .. Total

Init ==
    /\ token = "A"
    /\ pool = Total
    /\ loop = [i \in Inst |-> 0]
    /\ inTransit = 0

\* Pass the ring token to the other instance; always available.
Pass ==
    /\ token' = IF token = "A" THEN "B" ELSE "A"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, loop, inTransit>>

\* The token holder grabs an item from the shared pool into transit.
Grab(i) ==
    /\ token = i
    /\ pool > 0
    /\ pool' = pool - 1
    /\ inTransit' = inTransit + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, loop>>

\* The token holder deposits an item from transit into its own conveyor loop.
Deposit(i) ==
    /\ token = i
    /\ inTransit > 0
    /\ inTransit' = inTransit - 1
    /\ loop' = [loop EXCEPT ![i] = loop[i] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, pool>>

\* Release an item from a conveyor loop back to the shared pool.
Release(i) ==
    /\ loop[i] > 0
    /\ loop' = [loop EXCEPT ![i] = loop[i] - 1]
    /\ pool' = pool + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, inTransit>>

Next ==
    \/ Pass
    \/ \E i \in Inst : Grab(i) \/ Deposit(i) \/ Release(i)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Conservation: the shared pool, both conveyor loops, and transit always sum to the fixed total.
ItemsConserved == pool + loop["A"] + loop["B"] + inTransit = Total
====
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet runs two independent conveyor instances that share one item pool, with
exclusive handling of the pool granted by a ring token passed back and forth between the two
instances. The token holder grabs an item from the shared pool into transit, and then deposits the
in-transit item into its own conveyor loop. An item sitting in a conveyor loop may be released back
to the shared pool. Every item is always in exactly one of four places -- the shared pool, one of
the two instances' loops, or transit -- so no item is ever created or destroyed.

Actions: pass the ring token to the other instance; the token holder grabs an item from the shared
pool into transit; the token holder deposits an in-transit item into its own conveyor loop; release
an item from a conveyor loop back to the shared pool.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared pool, both conveyor loops, and the in-transit count always sum to the
fixed total number of items, so no item is ever created or destroyed.

---- MODULE W4Od19m5p4t4 ----
\* A library book-reservation system approves reservations by quorum vote. A book is proposed,
\* members vote, and a strict majority reserves it -- but only while the total number of
\* reservations is below a capacity that may be adjusted at runtime. The capacity is never lowered
\* below the number already reserved. Reservations may be cancelled. The number of reserved books
\* never exceeds the capacity bound.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Books == {0, 1, 2}
Members == {0, 1, 2}
NONE == 9
MaxCap == 3

VARIABLES reserved, candidate, votes, capacity

vars == <<reserved, candidate, votes, capacity>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ reserved \in SUBSET Books
    /\ candidate \in Books \cup {NONE}
    /\ votes \in SUBSET Members
    /\ capacity \in 0 .. MaxCap

Init ==
    /\ reserved = {}
    /\ candidate = NONE
    /\ votes = {}
    /\ capacity = MaxCap

\* Propose an unreserved book for a vote, resetting the tally.
Propose(b) ==
    /\ candidate = NONE
    /\ b \notin reserved
    /\ candidate' = b
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reserved, capacity>>

\* A member votes for the current candidate.
Vote(v) ==
    /\ candidate # NONE
    /\ v \notin votes
    /\ votes' = votes \cup {v}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reserved, candidate, capacity>>

\* A strict majority reserves the candidate, while under the capacity bound.
Reserve ==
    /\ candidate # NONE
    /\ 2 * Cardinality(votes) > Cardinality(Members)
    /\ Cardinality(reserved) < capacity
    /\ reserved' = reserved \cup {candidate}
    /\ candidate' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, capacity>>

\* Cancel a reservation.
Cancel(b) ==
    /\ b \in reserved
    /\ reserved' = reserved \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<candidate, votes, capacity>>

\* Capacity changes at runtime, but never below the number already reserved.
Resize(c) ==
    /\ c # capacity
    /\ c >= Cardinality(reserved)
    /\ capacity' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reserved, candidate, votes>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Books : Propose(b) \/ Cancel(b)
    \/ \E v \in Members : Vote(v)
    \/ Reserve
    \/ \E c \in 0 .. MaxCap : Resize(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Bounded capacity: the number of reserved books never exceeds the capacity bound.
WithinCap == Cardinality(reserved) <= capacity
====
nl:
A library book-reservation system approves reservations by quorum vote. An unreserved book is
proposed for a vote, which resets the tally; members then vote for the current candidate. Once a
strict majority has voted, the candidate book is reserved, but only while the total number of
reservations across the library is below a capacity that may be adjusted at runtime. The capacity
is never lowered below the number of books already reserved. Existing reservations may be cancelled.

Actions: propose an unreserved book for a vote, resetting the tally; a member votes for the
candidate; reserve the candidate given a strict majority and room under capacity; cancel a
reservation; resize the capacity at runtime, never below the number already reserved.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the total number of reserved books never exceeds the capacity bound.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od11m5p2t4 ----
\* A print-shop job spooler moves a fixed set of jobs through three stages: queued, printing, and
\* done. Starting a queued job printing requires a strict-majority quorum of operators and room
\* under a printing capacity that may change at runtime; starting consumes the quorum. Printing
\* jobs finish into done, and done jobs may be recycled to queued. Jobs are conserved: the three
\* stages always sum to the fixed total, none created or destroyed.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Operators == {0, 1, 2}
Total == 3
MaxCap == 3

VARIABLES queued, printing, done, votes, capacity

vars == <<queued, printing, done, votes, capacity>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ queued \in 0 .. Total
    /\ printing \in 0 .. Total
    /\ done \in 0 .. Total
    /\ votes \in SUBSET Operators
    /\ capacity \in 0 .. MaxCap

Init ==
    /\ queued = Total
    /\ printing = 0
    /\ done = 0
    /\ votes = {}
    /\ capacity = MaxCap

\* An operator votes to start the next job printing.
Vote(v) ==
    /\ v \notin votes
    /\ votes' = votes \cup {v}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queued, printing, done, capacity>>

\* Start a queued job printing: needs a strict-majority quorum and room under capacity; the quorum
\* is consumed.
StartPrint ==
    /\ queued > 0
    /\ 2 * Cardinality(votes) > Cardinality(Operators)
    /\ printing < capacity
    /\ queued' = queued - 1
    /\ printing' = printing + 1
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<done, capacity>>

\* A printing job finishes into done.
Finish ==
    /\ printing > 0
    /\ printing' = printing - 1
    /\ done' = done + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queued, votes, capacity>>

\* A done job is recycled back to queued (a reprint).
Recycle ==
    /\ done > 0
    /\ done' = done - 1
    /\ queued' = queued + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<printing, votes, capacity>>

\* Printing capacity changes at runtime to a different value; always available.
Resize(c) ==
    /\ c # capacity
    /\ capacity' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queued, printing, done, votes>>

Next ==
    \/ \E v \in Operators : Vote(v)
    \/ StartPrint
    \/ Finish
    \/ Recycle
    \/ \E c \in 0 .. MaxCap : Resize(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Conservation: queued, printing, and done jobs always sum to the fixed total.
JobsConserved == queued + printing + done = Total
====
nl:
A print-shop job spooler moves a fixed set of jobs through three stages: queued, printing, and
done. Operators vote to start the next job printing. Starting a queued job printing requires a
strict-majority quorum of operators and requires room below a printing capacity that may change at
runtime; starting the job consumes the quorum by clearing the votes. A printing job later finishes
into done, and a done job may be recycled back to queued for a reprint. No job is ever created or
destroyed.

Actions: an operator votes to start the next job; start a queued job printing given a strict
majority and room under capacity, consuming the quorum; finish a printing job into done; recycle a
done job back to queued; resize the printing capacity at runtime.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the counts of queued, printing, and done jobs always sum to the fixed total, so no
job is ever created or destroyed.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od12m8p2t1 ----
\* A blood-bank inventory tracker moves units between a loading dock and shelves inside a fridge,
\* guarded by hierarchical locks: a coarse fridge lock and a fine per-shelf lock. Holding both, a
\* worker stores a unit from the dock onto a shelf, or withdraws a unit from a shelf back to the
\* dock. Store and withdraw operations on different shelves interleave freely, so the underlying
\* messages may be applied in any order. Units are conserved: dock plus all shelves total a fixed
\* count, none created or destroyed.
EXTENDS Naturals

Shelves == {0, 1}
Workers == {0, 1}
FREE == 9
Total == 3

VARIABLES fridgeLock, shelfLock, units, dock, clock

vars == <<fridgeLock, shelfLock, units, dock, clock>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ fridgeLock \in Workers \cup {FREE}
    /\ shelfLock \in [Shelves -> Workers \cup {FREE}]
    /\ units \in [Shelves -> 0 .. Total]
    /\ dock \in 0 .. Total
    /\ clock \in {0, 1}

Init ==
    /\ fridgeLock = FREE
    /\ shelfLock = [s \in Shelves |-> FREE]
    /\ units = [s \in Shelves |-> 0]
    /\ dock = Total
    /\ clock = 0

\* Grab the coarse fridge lock.
GrabFridge(w) ==
    /\ fridgeLock = FREE
    /\ fridgeLock' = w
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelfLock, units, dock, clock>>

\* Grab a shelf's fine lock while holding the fridge lock.
GrabShelf(s, w) ==
    /\ fridgeLock = w
    /\ shelfLock[s] = FREE
    /\ shelfLock' = [shelfLock EXCEPT ![s] = w]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridgeLock, units, dock, clock>>

\* Store a unit from the dock onto a shelf, holding both locks.
Store(s, w) ==
    /\ fridgeLock = w
    /\ shelfLock[s] = w
    /\ dock > 0
    /\ dock' = dock - 1
    /\ units' = [units EXCEPT ![s] = units[s] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridgeLock, shelfLock, clock>>

\* Withdraw a unit from a shelf back to the dock, holding both locks.
Withdraw(s, w) ==
    /\ fridgeLock = w
    /\ shelfLock[s] = w
    /\ units[s] > 0
    /\ units' = [units EXCEPT ![s] = units[s] - 1]
    /\ dock' = dock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridgeLock, shelfLock, clock>>

\* Release a shelf lock.
ReleaseShelf(s, w) ==
    /\ shelfLock[s] = w
    /\ shelfLock' = [shelfLock EXCEPT ![s] = FREE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridgeLock, units, dock, clock>>

\* Release the fridge lock once no shelf is still locked by this worker.
ReleaseFridge(w) ==
    /\ fridgeLock = w
    /\ \A s \in Shelves : shelfLock[s] # w
    /\ fridgeLock' = FREE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelfLock, units, dock, clock>>

\* Housekeeping pulse; always available.
Tick ==
    /\ clock' = 1 - clock
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridgeLock, shelfLock, units, dock>>

Next ==
    \/ \E w \in Workers : GrabFridge(w) \/ ReleaseFridge(w)
    \/ \E s \in Shelves, w \in Workers :
         GrabShelf(s, w) \/ Store(s, w) \/ Withdraw(s, w) \/ ReleaseShelf(s, w)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Conservation: the dock plus all shelves always total the fixed unit count.
UnitsConserved == units[0] + units[1] + dock = Total
====
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker moves units between a loading dock and the shelves inside a fridge,
guarded by two levels of hierarchical locks: a coarse fridge lock and a fine per-shelf lock. While
holding both the fridge lock and a shelf's lock, a worker may store a unit from the dock onto that
shelf, or withdraw a unit from that shelf back to the dock. Store and withdraw operations on
different shelves interleave freely, so the underlying transfer messages may be applied in any
order. A worker cannot release the fridge lock while it still holds any shelf lock. A housekeeping
pulse ticks throughout. Every unit is always either on the dock or on exactly one shelf.

Actions: grab the coarse fridge lock; grab a shelf's fine lock while holding the fridge lock; store
a unit from the dock onto a shelf while holding both locks; withdraw a unit from a shelf back to the
dock while holding both locks; release a shelf lock; release the fridge lock once no shelf is still
locked by the worker; tick the housekeeping pulse.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the units on the dock plus the units on all shelves always total the fixed count,
so no unit is ever created or destroyed.
